name: Odin.Fun
rootCause: Odin.fun hemorrhaged $7 million on August 12th through basic AMM manipulation - their third breach in six months. PhD founder's credentials can't fix inadequate treasury or unclear compensation plans. The pattern feels disturbingly familiar.

descriptions.text: Odin.fun hemorrhaged $7 million on August 12th through basic AMM manipulation - their third breach in six months. PhD founder's credentials can't fix inadequate treasury or unclear compensation plans. The pattern feels disturbingly familiar.

The Bitcoin-based memecoin launchpad ODIN.FUN suffered an exploit, losing approximately 58.2 BTC (around $7 million). The attacker allegedly manipulated the prices of several tokens and then withdrew bitcoin based on the inflated values. On August 17, ODIN.FUN co-founder Bob Bodily stated: “Made great progress on funds today (as many of you already saw). 30+ BTC back into Odin. More funds in progress too.”

On August 12, 2025, Odin.fun suffered a $7M theft when attackers exploited an AMM vulnerability by depositing worthless memecoins, manipulating internal pool prices through self-trading, and withdrawing BTC liquidity at inflated rates. Odin.fun's AMM allowed liquidity pools and swaps to rely entirely on internal token balances, with no external price oracle, value parity checks, or controls against non-economically backed tokens. The system permitted self-trading and manipulation, enabling attackers to artificially inflate the price of worthless memecoins and withdraw disproportionate BTC.

Odin.fun, a bitcoin-based memecoin launchpad sort of like the popular pump.fun, was exploited for 58.2 BTC (~$7 million). The attacker had apparently manipulated the price of various tokens, then withdrew bitcoin based on the inflated prices. A team member suggested they were unsure of the total amount stolen, "but as of right now, our company treasury isn't big enough to cover the losses".
